solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

blocks.note: first meaning: Portuguese stinging sea creatures with that name
second meaning: people who favour military action, warmongers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawks' tempts you towards birds, but here they are aggressive politicians, the opposite of doves. The Portuguese man-of-war is a floating stinger often called a jellyfish.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural names both the stinging Portuguese marine creatures and belligerent people, as well as old warships, so both senses fit.

blocks.note: a bill before parliament is a proposed measure
S is the standard abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Someone called Bill has dainty little hands, and other small features.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name, but it is a piece of legislation. A hand is a unit of four inches, still used for the height of horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is a unit of length, so hands, feet, inches and the like are all units of measurement.

blocks.note: first meaning: the south wind of Greek mythology
second meaning: a denial that we were responsible, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is someone denying blame for breaking wind. Read as two words the answer is the denial 'not us!'; as one word it is the Greek god of the south wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Notus was the ancient Greek personification of the south wind, brother of Boreas and Zephyrus.

blocks.note: surface reading: artwork created on a computer or tablet
setter's reading: done with the digits, meaning the fingers

explanation.walkthrough: Digital now suggests computers, but a digit is a finger, so digital art is pictures made by smearing paint with the hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Children's pictures made by dabbing paint on with the fingertips are art produced with the digits.

indicators.note: a jacket is the outer layer, so taking it off strips away the outermost letters at each end

blocks.note: a rambler is someone who walks the countryside for pleasure

explanation.surface: A hiker has shed their coat while out on a stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the first and last letters of RAMBLER leaves AMBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to stroll at a slow, relaxed pace, a leisurely kind of walking.

blocks.note: surface reading: some achievement or trophy that signals triumph
setter's reading: a literal written mark, the one a teacher puts beside a correct answer

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase suggests a status symbol, but the mark is a pen stroke on homework showing an answer is right.
explanation.definitionFit: A check mark written beside a correct answer literally marks that the pupil succeeded.

clue.text: Hire store will founder, I suppose

definitions.note: the definition is what this person would say, standing for the speaker rather than a noun

indicators.note: to founder is to collapse or sink, so the letters break apart and settle in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A rental shop owner predicts the business is going under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Founder' reads as the person who started the shop, but it is the verb meaning to sink. The definition is a cryptic one: someone who says 'I suppose' all the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who speculates and forms hypotheses keeps supposing things, so 'I suppose' is their catchphrase.

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a rusty skill is out of practice and needs brushing up

explanation.surface: A grumpy old Tory whose skills could do with refreshing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brush-up' suggests grooming an untidy old gent, but it means revising a skill that has gone out of practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusty person is irritable and gruff in manner, much like someone bad-tempered and sullen.

clue.text: Dream offered by a chain letter is dodgy

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable and not in proper order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A chain letter promises riches, but the scheme is suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: A chain letter does sell a fantasy of easy riches, which is what makes the surface so smooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle in the air is an idiom for an impractical scheme or daydream that will never come true.

clue.text: Continue to haul box full of goods

blocks.note: to cart something is to haul or carry it
as in 'go on', meaning carry on

explanation.surface: Someone keeps lugging a heavy box of merchandise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' here means attached to: ON is added to the end of CART.
explanation.definitionFit: A carton is a cardboard packing container in which goods are shipped or sold.

clue.text: Dominate a match in which one appears to be falling apart

indicators.note: something appearing inside another thing sits within it, so one piece goes into the middle of the other

blocks.note: to be ten up, ten points or goals ahead, is to dominate a game
A is one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A sports report about a winning side that still seems to be collapsing.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as BE A TEN UP: being ten up is dominating a match, with A (one) slotted in. The surface contradiction of dominating while falling apart is the hook.
explanation.definitionFit: A beaten-up car or chair is battered and dilapidated, in poor condition and close to falling apart.

blocks.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
US for the United States, hence American
S is the abbreviation for soprano in music

explanation.surface: Someone curses about a singer from the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a reversal or container signal, but here it is simply C for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: To cuss is an informal, chiefly American, verb meaning to curse or use bad language.

indicators.note: when a word changes, its letters are reorganised into another form
going around something means enclosing it on both sides

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange
EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: Voters put up with changes being made to their town.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postal district of the City of London, the financial district, a crossword staple for 'city'.
explanation.definitionFit: The electorate is the whole body of people entitled to vote in an election.

blocks.note: first meaning: calf-length trousers originally designed for cycling
second meaning: cyclists, who shift gears as they ride

explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing gear' suggests clothes to change into, which fits trousers, but it is cyclists shifting gears on their bikes.
explanation.definitionFit: The cropped trousers were named after cyclists, and riders literally push the pedals with their feet.

clue.text: Passages from law essay I misread

indicators.note: reading something wrongly garbles it, so these letters come out in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone quotes extracts from a legal essay they got wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passages' looks like extracts from the essay, but it means corridors.
explanation.definitionFit: Aisleways are walkways between rows of seats or shelves, the sense of passages as corridors.

clue.text: In the evening, drop of plonk

blocks.note: first meaning: to put down
second meaning: to put something down heavily

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a glass of cheap wine at dusk; plonk is British slang for cheap wine. Here it is the verb. 'In the evening' also hints at the sun, which has set by then.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something down, drop it and plonk it are all ways of placing an object somewhere.

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to be in a suit is to be wearing it

explanation.surface: A son working in the family undertaker's business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undertaking' suggests funerals, and 'in' looks like a container signal; it is actually WEARING, as in dressed in.
explanation.definitionFit: Swearing an oath is solemnly promising, and an undertaking is a formal pledge to do something.

blocks.note: first meaning: Scotland's oldest university
second meaning: the famous golf course, the home of golf

explanation.walkthrough: 'University course' looks like a degree programme, but it is two separate things sharing one Scottish town's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fife town has both an ancient university and the Old Course, the most famous golf links in the world.

clue.text: Fix that a late don might be in?

definitions.text: that a late don might be in

blocks.note: first meaning: to bind firmly or secure

blocks.clueFragment: that a late don might be in
blocks.note: second meaning: what a murdered Mafia boss might be encased in, dumped in the river

explanation.walkthrough: A 'late don' sounds like a tardy Oxford tutor, but it is a dead Mafia boss wearing concrete overshoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cement is the binding building material that holds bricks and stones together, and gangsters notoriously used it on victims.

definitions.note: an anniversary name standing for the ordinal; part of speech differs

indicators.note: metal that is melted down loses its shape and is recast into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A gang of robbers melts down stolen platinum.
explanation.walkthrough: Platinum looks like the loot, but it is the name for an anniversary, such as a platinum jubilee.
explanation.definitionFit: A platinum jubilee or anniversary marks seventy years, so platinum stands for that milestone.

indicators.note: saying something is not there means it is left out of the word

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
Greta Thunberg, the Swedish climate campaigner
the letter to be dropped

explanation.surface: An English environmental campaigner who is no high achiever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a high-flyer' reads as a put-down, but 'not a' removes the final A from GRETA and 'high-flyer' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a heron-like wading bird, and any bird in the sky is literally a flyer up high.

indicators.note: something that eats takes food inside itself, so one piece swallows another

blocks.note: in jazz slang a cat is a man, a guy
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A cat devours an aged fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Carp looks like the fish being eaten, but it is the verb to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to complain or find fault persistently, just as one would grumble or whinge.

clue.text: Some sit fuming about legal expert

indicators.note: 'some' means only a part, so the letters are a portion lifted from within the words
turning about means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Some people sit seething over a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the letters backwards from the middle of 'sit fuming'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mufti is a Muslim scholar who issues rulings on Islamic law, hence an expert in law.

indicators.note: making one thing into another converts it, so one letter is swapped for a new one

blocks.note: to keep something is to retain it
D is the abbreviation for daughter
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A household servant keeps making the daughter run errands.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the D at the end of RETAINED for R.
explanation.definitionFit: A retainer is an old word for a servant who has long served a family or household.

indicators.note: to flip something over is to turn it the other way round

blocks.note: FA, short for sweet FA, is British slang for nothing at all
just and fair both mean equitable

explanation.surface: An exasperated complaint that nothing is happening, it is all just business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British oath, but it turns FA round. Sweet FA is a British euphemism for 'nothing at all'.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair can mean a matter or concern, as in 'that's my business', so the words are synonyms.

indicators.note: 'in' means located inside, so the letters sit within the word that follows

blocks.note: the run of letters inside this town's name

explanation.surface: A sweet-maker based in a town on Tyneside.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town in north-east England, across the river from Newcastle. The definition is an obscure proper name, so the hidden letters do the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Presumably the setter intends a confectionery maker or brand by this name; it is rare, so the hidden letters confirm it.

indicators.note: being about something means surrounding it on every side

blocks.note: staring is looking fixedly
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A vocalist who appears to be around fifty years old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' suggests a pop star, but here it is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The starling is a common songbird known for its varied chattering song and mimicry.
